plan.p0: A plausible rule is diagonal-skeleton extraction: retain the singleton diagonal colors (7 in both examples), erase compact non-diagonal components, and add parallel diagonals so each such component contributes a track associated with the nearest original diagonal. The distinguishing assumption is that component count, rather than exact shape or color, determines added tracks.
plan.p1: A plausible rule is obstacle-to-ray conversion: treat each compact component as an obstacle intersecting or bordering a diagonal marker, remove it, and continue the marker as diagonal rays through selected obstacle corners. The distinguishing assumption is that bounding-box corner geometry selects the new offsets; a differently shaped component would therefore change the tracks.
plan.p2: A plausible rule is global diagonal completion: erase all compact colors and preserve marker diagonals, then add every parallel diagonal whose offset is supported by the combined diagonal span of the compact objects. The distinguishing assumption is that objects are pooled globally, so changing one object can alter tracks associated with another marker or orientation.
plan.p3: A plausible rule is color- and orientation-specific encoding: each singleton diagonal color specifies a family of offsets, while nearby compact shapes determine which members are emitted; the output keeps only those colored diagonals. The distinguishing assumption is that color identity matters, so swapping colors or using a new marker color could produce a different family even with identical geometry.
